about: What to measure and which site constants an annual energy, cost and CO2e estimate needs, per question, and where each constant comes from. Public typical values are used only with --use-defaults and always labelled. See docs/IMPACT_ESTIMATE.md.

questions.question: Is this pump throttled by a control valve when it could run on a variable speed drive?
questions.note: Pump on a variable speed drive: measured kW before and after. Before installing, the after kW can only be estimated from the flow-duration curve, the pump curve and the static head; say so.

measure.what: Average electrical input kW before and after (or the kW reduction): a clamp-on three-phase power meter, the drive or MCC power reading, or the historian's motor kW tag, over a representative period at the same production rate. An estimate from curves (pump/fan curve and affinity laws) must say so.
Operating hours per year the change applies: historian run status, the operating schedule, or maintenance records. Not 8,760 unless it really runs all year.
Optional: the reduction in billing-peak kW (interval meter data at the billing interval) and the months it applies.

constants.name: Electricity energy price
constants.where: Your electricity bill and rate schedule: the energy charge per kWh in the hours the change applies (weight time-of-use periods by the hours saved in each). Not total bill / total kWh, which mixes in demand and fixed charges.
constants.public_typical_value: EIA Electric Power Annual Table 2.4, US average industrial price (2025)

constants.name: Grid emission factor
constants.where: Location-based Scope 2: the EPA eGRID total output emission rate (CO2e) for your eGRID subregion; find the subregion by ZIP code in EPA's Power Profiler, then read the rate from the eGRID summary tables. Market-based Scope 2 instead uses your utility's published supplier-specific emission factor or your contract instruments (RECs, PPAs). Subregion rates differ about 5 times.
constants.public_typical_value: EPA eGRID2023 US total output CO2e rate

constants.name: Demand charge (only to estimate a demand kW reduction)
constants.where: Your electricity bill and rate schedule: the demand charge per kW per month, its billing interval (often 15 minutes) and any ratchet clause. A kW reduction saves demand charges only if it lowers the billing peak; check against interval meter data. Never defaulted.
